clue.text: Flutters inside this place of business

definitions.text: Flutters inside this place of business

parts.words: Flutters inside this place of business
parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet, so this is the high-street premises where people go in to place wagers rather than somewhere birds flap about

explanation.surface: Something is fluttering about inside a shop or office.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's premises is where punters place small wagers, which Britons call flutters.

clue.text: Bay leaves, or some sort of mango, first showing flowers on the tree

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each word from Bay to mango is shown, spelling out the answer in turn

explanation.surface: A remark about bay leaves or a kind of mango tree coming into flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first showing' takes the initial letter of each of the seven words from 'Bay' to 'mango'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the mass of flowers that appears on a fruit tree in spring.

clue.text: We don't often get good time like this

definitions.text: We don't often get good time like this

parts.words: We don't often get good time like this
parts.note: reads like a grumble about rare good weather or timekeeping, but describes a pleasant indulgence enjoyed only occasionally

explanation.surface: A complaint that good times are rare.
explanation.definitionFit: A special indulgence is by nature an occasional good time, not an everyday one.

clue.text: The emphatic type, as were

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The emphatic type, as were' (7): 'The emphatic type' defines ITALICS, but 'as were' gives no letters or sense; probably a word lost in OCR (perhaps 'as it were'), no scan to check.

clue.text: Eats fast, and makes a noise!

definitions.meaning: the throaty call a turkey makes

explanation.surface: Someone bolts their food and is noisy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfing food is one sense; the other is the sound a male turkey produces.

clue.text: End the ear trouble, thus being given encouragement

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of these three words are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ending an earache, and so feeling cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ENDTHEEAR; 'thus' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be heartened is to be cheered and given fresh courage.

clue.text: Starts a book, often, but never finishes it

definitions.text: Starts a book, often, but never finishes it

parts.words: Starts a book, often, but never finishes it
parts.note: sounds like a lazy reader who abandons novels, but describes the introductory section placed at the front of many volumes

explanation.surface: A reader who keeps beginning books and giving up.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction at the front of a volume opens it and is never found at the end.

clue.text: Volcanic hole rarely contains disease

indicators.note: the run of words holds the answer within it, spanning the end of one word into the next two

explanation.surface: A rarely seen volcanic crater harbours infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' signals the answer sitting inside 'volcaniC HOLE RArely'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute bacterial infection of the gut spread by contaminated water.

clue.text: Funny company for a monarch to keep!

definitions.text: Funny company for a monarch to keep!

parts.words: Funny company for a monarch to keep!
parts.note: funny suggests odd associates, but it means amusing: the royal household's professional entertainer

explanation.surface: A remark that a king keeps strange company.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or jester was retained in a royal household to amuse the sovereign.

clue.text: At verbs' translation, appears most courageous

indicators.note: a translation carries words into another form, so these letters are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson where translating verbs looks heroic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges ATVERBS; 'appears' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of brave: having the greatest courage.

clue.text: American might find its nerve-centre here

definitions.text: American might find its nerve-centre here

parts.words: American might find its nerve-centre here
parts.note: might looks like a verb (an American may find), but is a noun: US military power has its headquarters building here

explanation.surface: An American may discover where his nerves are centred.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building in Virginia is headquarters of the US Department of Defense.

clue.text: Being knocked over, was a bit distressed

explanation.surface: Someone knocked down and rather shaken by it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an overturned state and emotional disturbance.

clue.text: Unwell but comfortable? Not comfortable in mind!

parts.note: being unwell means being ill
comfortable means relaxed, at ease

explanation.surface: A paradox: how can one be sick and yet comfortable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word; the two halves seem to contradict, yet together mean uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone uneasy and anxious.

clue.text: Some of the head places for religious folk

definitions.meaning: the flat parts on each side of the skull, beside the eyes

explanation.surface: Part of the head and places of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the sides of the forehead and houses of worship share this name.

clue.text: Be prone to set an ambush?

definitions.text: Be prone to set an ambush?

parts.words: Be prone to set an ambush?
parts.note: be prone to suggests having a tendency, but here it means literally lying flat, ready to spring a trap

explanation.surface: Someone with a habit of laying ambushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide ready to attack, as an ambusher does, often lying down.

clue.text: The pretender isn't this because the Queen comes back

parts.note: since means because

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the Queen returns, so it is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for the Queen

explanation.surface: A pretender to the throne is shown up when the monarch returns.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a pretender to the throne is by nature not genuine, which the surface's royal story disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is false, the opposite of genuine and honest.

clue.text: They symbolise badges, maybe

definitions.meaning: things that stand for an idea

explanation.surface: Badges may stand for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbolic devices and heraldic or worn insignia both go by this word.

clue.text: In this condition, likely to be snappy under pressure

definitions.text: In this condition, likely to be snappy under pressure

parts.words: In this condition, likely to be snappy under pressure
parts.note: snappy suggests irritable when stressed, but means liable to snap when pressed

explanation.surface: A person who gets short-tempered when stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard but fragile breaks easily when force is applied.

clue.text: Being financially OK may cause things to melt

definitions.meaning: a liquid that dissolves other substances

explanation.surface: Wealth that makes problems dissolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Means able to pay debts, and also a dissolving liquid.

clue.text: Discerned how the cheque was written?

definitions.meaning: a cheque is drawn up in a payee's name

explanation.surface: Spotting how a cheque had been filled in.
explanation.definitionFit: Means perceived, and also filled in to a named payee, as a cheque is.

clue.text: Mum's vehicle gets a cosmetic

parts.note: Ma is mum, so Mum's is MA'S
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Mother's car comes with some make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up applied to darken eyelashes.

clue.text: An eye specialist cuts oil out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An optician cuts down on oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for an ophthalmologist or optician.

clue.text: Rings late, about cornered percussion instruments

indicators.note: about here means around in a jumble, so the letters are moved round into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rings late about musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-sided metal bars struck in the orchestra, so with corners.

clue.text: A hundred take a breather, having held on tight

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a lung is the organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: A hundred people pause for breath after holding on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' and 'having' are link words; 'breather' is not a rest but the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of cling: gripped firmly.

clue.text: Sounds like money for the store

indicators.note: says the word for money is pronounced the same as the answer

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A remark that money sounds right for the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden stock or hoard.

clue.text: Follow one's steps back to take another copy?

definitions.meaning: go back over the route taken

explanation.surface: Retracing one's route to make another copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Means go back over a route, and humorously trace a second time.

clue.text: Get a lot for your money at one

definitions.text: Get a lot for your money at one

parts.words: Get a lot for your money at one
parts.note: a lot sounds like plenty of value, but is a numbered item for sale at a saleroom

explanation.surface: Somewhere you get good value for your cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale where items, called lots, go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: One building his career? More than that!

definitions.text: One building his career? More than that!

parts.words: One building his career? More than that!
parts.note: building his career suggests ambition, but this person makes a living from buildings and land, selling properties

explanation.surface: An ambitious careerist, and then some.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who sells houses and property on clients' behalf.
